Definition: from ἐράω (to love); beloved; Erastus, a Christian:--Erastus.
BiblicalUsage: Érastos — Erastus — was a companion of Paul, sent with Timothy into Macedonia, and later the chamberlain of Corinth. He is named in Acts and in Romans, and again in Timothy, where Paul says Erastus stayed at Corinth. His fuller story is on his People profile.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Erastus matters because he is the faithful helper, not the headline name: sent, stayed, and named by Paul with honour. I hold that the church runs on men like him.
RelatedEvents: Paul's Missionary Journeys; The Riot at Ephesus
